title: BDD/FC conjecture
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: Is every finite set \(R\) of existential tuple-generating dependencies with bounded derivation depth finitely controllable? Use the precise query-rewriting definition of bounded derivation depth below. The required conclusion is that for every finite database \(I\) and every Boolean conjunctive query \(q\), \[(I,R)\models q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(I,R)\models_{\mathrm{fin}}q.\] The left side quantifies over all models extending \(I\) and satisfying \(R\); the right side quantifies only over finite such models. The conjecture quantifies over every finite relational signature of arbitrary finite arities, and permits conjunctions of several atoms in rule heads.
why: Bounded derivation depth permits queries under existential rules to be answered through finite positive rewritings on the original database. Finite controllability asks whether considering only finite possible worlds changes those answers. Connecting the two would clarify when this useful query-processing property also supports finite-model semantics, across arbitrary relational arities.
status_note: The general conjecture is explicitly open in the checked PODS 2025 paper, which was posted to arXiv in March 2026. Its structural theorem does not imply full finite controllability, and the original binary-signature theorem assumes single-head rules. Bounded later-work checks through 2026-09-15 found no resolution of the unrestricted target; the review is not an exhaustive proof or literature certification.

progress.text: Gogacz and Marcinkowski pose the BDD/FC conjecture and establish their binary-signature, single-head result at PODS. The saved arXiv version was posted in August 2014.

Larroque, Ostropolski-Nalewaja and Thomazo publish a structural property of BDD rule sets in Proc. ACM Management of Data 3(2), article 101, for PODS 2025; the general conjecture remains open in their introduction.
The PODS 2025 paper is posted to arXiv. Its abstract describes the theorem as a step toward the conjecture, and its full introduction explicitly says it does not establish the conjecture.

sentences: The BDD/FC conjecture asks whether every finite existential rule set with bounded derivation depth is finitely controllable.
Bounded derivation depth is expressed by a finite positive rewriting for each conjunctive query that works on every database.
Finite controllability means that a query failing in some unrestricted model also fails in a finite model.
The question allows arbitrary finite relational arities and several atoms in a rule head.
The known binary theorem requires single-head rules, and the checked PODS 2025 result posted in 2026 leaves the general conjecture open.

definitions: A relational signature is a finite collection of relation symbols, each with a fixed nonnegative integer arity. An atom has the form \(P(t_1,\ldots,t_a)\), with repeated arguments allowed. In rules and queries the arguments are variables; there are no function symbols, built-in equality or inequality, negation, or interpreted order. A rule is the sentence \(\forall\bar x\,\forall\bar y\,(B(\bar x,\bar y)\to\exists\bar z\,H(\bar y,\bar z))\), where \(B,H\) are finite nonempty conjunctions of atoms, each universal variable occurs in \(B\), and the only universal variables in \(H\) come from \(\bar y\). The tuples of universal and existential variables are disjoint. The existential tuple may be empty, so ordinary positive Datalog rules are included. A rule set is finite, and rule heads may contain several atoms. A database \(I\) is a finite set of relational facts on finitely many named distinct elements; its active domain is the set of elements appearing in these facts. Empty active domains and nullary facts are allowed. A model extending \(I\) has a nonempty domain containing its named elements and includes every fact of \(I\); it may add elements and facts, including new facts on old elements. It satisfies \(R\) with ordinary first-order semantics, and must preserve the identities of the named database elements. “Finite model” means a finite domain, with no prescribed cardinality bound. A conjunctive query \(q(\bar u)=\exists\bar v\,A(\bar u,\bar v)\) uses a finite nonempty conjunction of relational atoms, with every displayed free variable occurring in an atom. A Boolean query has no free variables. A union of conjunctive queries is a finite disjunction of such queries with the same free variables; the empty disjunction denotes false. Query evaluation on a database means a variable assignment into its active domain satisfying all required facts, and for a union means satisfaction of at least one disjunct. For an answer tuple \(\bar a\) from the active domain, \((I,R)\models q(\bar a)\) means that every model extending \(I\) and satisfying \(R\) satisfies this instantiated query. Define \(R\) to have bounded derivation depth if for every conjunctive query \(q(\bar u)\) there is a finite union of conjunctive queries \(Q(\bar u)\) over the same signature such that, for every finite database \(I\) and every compatible answer tuple \(\bar a\), \((I,R)\models q(\bar a)\) if and only if \(I\models Q(\bar a)\). The rewriting \(Q\) may depend on \(R,q\) but not on the database or answer tuple. This is the source’s equivalent positive query-rewriting formulation of bounded derivation depth; it does not require one depth bound for all queries. Finite controllability is the displayed unrestricted-versus-finite equivalence for every \(I,q\). There is no syntactic guardedness, stickiness, binary-arity or single-head restriction on \(R\), and no time bound for constructing a rewriting or countermodel.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the implication for every finite signature and rule set, or refute it. A positive answer must show that whenever a Boolean conjunctive query fails in some possibly infinite model of \(I,R\), it also fails in some finite model of the same database and rules, assuming only the stated bounded derivation depth property. A negative answer must provide one finite signature and rule set \(R\), prove its rewriting property for every conjunctive query, and provide a finite database \(I\) and Boolean conjunctive query \(q\) such that every finite model of \(I,R\) satisfies \(q\) but some infinite model does not. Showing bounded behavior for a single query does not establish the premise on \(R\). A counterexample whose rules lack bounded derivation depth, or a theorem for binary single-head rules alone, does not settle this target.

context_blocks.text: Amarilli’s source page states the implication using positive query rewriting and finite-model entailment. The named BDD/FC conjecture originates in Gogacz and Marcinkowski’s work, which supplies the formal definitions behind that summary.

Gogacz and Marcinkowski prove the implication for binary signatures under their convention that tuple-generating dependencies have single-atom heads. Their Section 5.3 explicitly discusses the multi-head issue. Thus the source page’s shorter “binary signature” summary must be read with the head restriction; arbitrary multi-head binary rules are not covered by that theorem.

Larroque, Ostropolski-Nalewaja and Thomazo’s 2025 paper uses general existential rules and records the equivalence between bounded derivation depth and UCQ rewritability as Proposition 4. Its introduction explicitly leaves the unrestricted BDD/FC conjecture open.

Their Theorem 1 establishes a structural implication about arbitrarily large directed cliques and a self-loop query for BDD rule sets. The authors expressly distinguish this partial result from the full finite-controllability conjecture. The March 2026 arXiv posting is a posting of this PODS 2025 work, not a newly claimed complete proof.
